## Verdicts for analysis lines the migrated database cannot settle.
##
## bootstrap_work_file.py classifies most lines mechanically -- an XML record
## from its own text, a field line from a measurement against the migrated
## database. What is left is a DEL field whose column still holds its 19.0
## values, or a NEW one uniform on a populated table: a QUESTION, which only
## reading 20.0's source can answer.
##
## Each verdict below was reached that way and says what was FOUND, not that
## somebody looked. A line with no entry here is written into the work file as
## "# NEEDS A VERDICT", so `grep -c "NEEDS A VERDICT"` counts exactly the debt.
##
## Format: a module:model.field key on its own line, its marker lines, a blank
## line. Lines starting ## are comments and are not part of any marker.

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 20.0 removes the concept: there is no field anywhere in 20.0 to carry into
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## hr -- measured against erp_mig20test (the sanitised prod copy) 2026-10-02.
## That database carries 2 employees, 2 versions and 0 jobs, which is thinner
## than the seed this work file was bootstrapped against (siblings above cite
## 25 / 31 / 9). Where a verdict rests on counted rows it says so; where the
## seed is too thin to prove anything, it says that instead.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

hr:hr.version.tz
# SCRIPT NEEDED: every version came out UTC where every employee is
# America/New_York, and the real value is still in the database. 19.0 declared
# hr.version.tz related='employee_id.tz' (hr_version.py:153), so nothing was
# stored on the version -- the value lived in resource_resource.tz. 20.0
# inverts the relation: hr.version.tz is stored and required with
# default=env.context tz or env.user.tz or 'UTC' (hr_version.py:162), and
# hr.employee.tz becomes related="version_id.tz" (hr_employee.py:309). So the
# upgrade had to materialise it and took the default instead. Measured: both
# migrated versions hold 'UTC' while the resources behind their employees hold
# 'America/New_York'. Nothing re-derives it -- _get_tz() returns self.tz first
# (hr_version.py:715-717) -- so the wrong zone reaches _get_resources_per_tz
# and every working-hours and attendance calculation downstream, a four or five
# hour shift. post-migration must fill hr_version.tz from resource_resource.tz
# through hr_employee.resource_id, and report any version it cannot source

hr:hr.job.user_id
# SCRIPT NEEDED: 20.0's recruiter_id is this field retyped, not a new one. Both
# are labelled "Recruiter" and carry the same help text word for word; only the
# comodel changed, res.users -> hr.employee. The 19.0 column survives in
# hr_job, so pre-migration should keep it under a legacy name and
# post-migration set recruiter_id to the hr.employee whose user_id matches,
# reporting any recruiter with no employee record. hr_job holds 0 rows on this
# copy, so nothing here exercises it

hr:hr.version.departure_reason_id
# SCRIPT NEEDED: what stops is the reading, not the data. 19.0 stored
# departure_reason_id, departure_description and departure_date on hr_version;
# 20.0 moves all three onto the new hr.employee.departure and makes
# hr.version's related through departure_id, so the surviving hr_version
# columns go invisible to the ORM -- hr_employee_departure holds 0 rows and
# every hr_version.departure_id is NULL. post-migration should create one
# hr.employee.departure per version holding any of the three and point
# hr_version.departure_id at it. All three are NULL on both copies' versions,
# so this copy cannot show the loss

hr:hr.version.departure_description
# SCRIPT NEEDED: carried by the same script as departure_reason_id above. 20.0
# reads it through departure_id.departure_description, so the 19.0 hr_version
# column is orphaned unless an hr.employee.departure row is built from it

hr:hr.employee.study_school
# NOTHING TO DO: nothing was entered. 20.0 keeps study_field ("Field of Study")
# but has no School field, and count(*), count(study_school) on hr_employee is
# 2|0 before the upgrade and 2|0 after -- the column survives, because the ORM
# does not drop it, holding NULL on every row

hr:hr.employee.birthday_month
# NOTHING TO DO: 20.0 fills it itself. It is store=True
# compute='_compute_birthday_month', writing str(birthday.month) or else '0'
# (hr_employee.py:589-591). birthday is NULL on both employees and
# birthday_month came out '0', the "Not specified" key -- the right answer for
# an unknown birthday, so the compute ran

hr:hr.employee.contract_template_id
# NOTHING TO DO: 19.0 had no column here -- hr.employee got the field by
# _inherits from hr.version, and the 19.0 hr_employee table carries no
# contract_template_id. The value lived in hr_version.contract_template_id,
# which survives untouched and is NULL on both versions either side of the
# upgrade. 20.0's own stored Many2one on hr.employee is UI staging for the
# template button rather than a record of truth, so a NULL is correct

hr:hr.employee.hr_presence_state
# NOTHING TO DO: nothing was ever stored for the dropped key to invalidate.
# Both versions declare it compute='_compute_presence_state' with no store, and
# information_schema returns 0 columns named hr_presence_state across
# hr_employee and hr_employee_public. 19.0's 'archive' value was derived from
# the employee being inactive, which `active` still records

hr:hr.departure.reason.active
# NOTHING TO DO: 20.0 adds the archive flag where 19.0 had none, and its
# default True is what every carried row holds -- count(*), count(active),
# count(*) where active is 4|4|4, so the upgrade archived no reason

hr:hr.job.company_id
# NOTHING TO DO on this data, and it cannot be proven in general here: hr_job
# holds 0 rows either side, so the NOT NULL applied over an empty table and
# defaulted nothing. 19.0 already defaulted company_id to env.company
# (hr_job.py:39), so a NULL was only reachable by writing one deliberately

hr:hr.version.resource_calendar_id
# NOTHING TO DO: no row came out wrong -- both versions hold
# resource_calendar_id = 1 before and after, matching
# resource_resource.calendar_id = 1 for both employees' resources. The copy
# cannot prove the mechanism, because res_company 1's resource_calendar_id is
# also 1, so the 20.0 default would have written the same number

hr:mail.activity.technical_usage
# NOTHING TO DO: the core field is new in 20.0, so there are no 19.0 values for
# hr's two added keys to invalidate -- technical_usage appears nowhere under
# 19.0's addons, and 20.0's mail declares it selection=[('none', 'Non

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## point_of_sale -- measured against erp_mig20test (the sanitised prod copy)
## 2026-10-02. POS is barely used there: 1 pos_config, 10 pos_payment_method,
## and 0 rows in pos_session, pos_order, pos_payment, pos_category, pos_preset;
## pos_restaurant is uninstalled. Neighbouring lines above cite counts from an
## earlier demo-loaded run. Where a verdict rests on source rather than on rows,
## it says so.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

point_of_sale:pos.config.invoice_journal_id
# SCRIPT NEEDED: carry it into journal_id, whose meaning changed underneath it.
# In 19.0 invoice_journal_id was the journal for POS invoices (pos_order.py:919)
# and journal_id was the closing journal. In 20.0 _prepare_invoice_vals reads
# config_id.journal_id (pos_order.py:1557). Nothing moved the value: the one row
# still holds journal_id = 19 and invoice_journal_id = 1. Journal 1 (INV, sale,
# created 2020-01-05) carries all 88 POS invoice moves; journal 19 (POSS, sale,
# created 2020-01-06) carries 0. So after the upgrade POS invoices are cut in a
# journal with no history instead of the one holding every POS invoice to date

point_of_sale:pos.config.closing_journal_id
# SCRIPT NEEDED: carry the old journal_id into it -- the precompute invented a
# new journal rather than reusing the one 19.0 posted to. 19.0 posted the
# session closing entry to config.journal_id (pos_session.py:819); 20.0 posts it
# to config.closing_journal_id (pos_session.py:988).
# _compute_closing_journal_id calls _ensure_company_closing_journal(), which
# creates a POSC journal: the migrated row holds closing_journal_id = 88, whose
# create_date is 2026-10-01 -- the migration run itself -- while journal_id is
# still 19, the journal 19.0 would have posted to. The script must only carry
# journals of type 'sale': 19.0's domain was ('general','sale') and 20.0's is
# ('sale',) alone. Journal 19 qualifies

point_of_sale:pos.config.session_closing_mode
# SCRIPT NEEDED: write 'closing' on every pre-existing config -- the default
# 'daily' changes WHEN accounting entries are generated. 19.0 built the closing
# entry only when a session was closed and shipped no cron for it. 20.0 ships
# point_of_sale.ir_cron_pos_auto_order_invoicing, active, every 10 minutes, and
# its _launch_cron_generate_invoice_period selects ('config_id.
# session_closing_mode', '=', 'daily') and calls _validate_session_accounting on
# sessions that are still open. The migrated row holds 'daily' with
# session_closing_daily_hour 4.0, so an upgraded database starts posting session
# accounting at 04:00 whether or not anyone closed the session. 'closing' is
# 20.0's spelling of what 19.0 did. The copy cannot show the effect -- the lab
# disables every cron -- so the 20.0 data file is the evidence

point_of_sale:pos.payment.currency_rate
# SCRIPT NEEDED: fill it from pos_order.currency_rate. 19.0 declared it
# related='pos_order_id.currency_rate' with no store, so there was no column and
# every read went to the order; 20.0 declares a plain stored Float
# (pos_payment.py:39) and nothing fills it for historical rows. The source is
# intact -- pos.order.currency_rate is a stored compute in both versions and the
# column survives -- so UPDATE pos_payment p SET currency_rate = o.currency_rate
# FROM pos_order o WHERE o.id = p.pos_order_id reproduces what 19.0 returned.
# pos_payment has 0 rows here

point_of_sale:pos.session.move_id
# SCRIPT NEEDED: carry it into account_move.pos_session_sales_id. 19.0 kept the
# session's closing entry as one many2one on pos.session (pos_session.py:88);
# 20.0 inverts the link and splits it across pos_session_sales_id,
# pos_session_refunds_id and pos_session_correction_id on account.move. The work
# file already records all three new columns as empty on every row, while the
# old move_id column survives with its FK intact, so the link is recoverable
# with one UPDATE into pos_session_sales_id (19.0 posted sales and refunds into
# one move). Not cosmetic: 20.0's _compute_always_tax_exigible depends on
# pos_session_ids and forces always_tax_exigible True for a move belonging to a
# session, so unlinked historical closing moves can recompute to the wrong
# exigibility. pos_session is empty here

point_of_sale:pos.payment.method.type
# DONE: post-migration fills it from the journal, which is 19.0's own rule.
# 19.0's type was a NON-stored compute (pos_payment_method.py:59) so there was
# no column; 20.0 declares it stored and required. The script replays 19.0's
# _compute_type verbatim. The five rows NAMED "Bank" came out 'pay_later', not
# 'bank', because their journal_id is NULL -- and that is what 19.0 displayed
# for them too: they are 2020-vintage records from the era when a non-cash
# method was is_cash_count=False with no journal. Writing 'bank' would be an
# invention -- 20.0's form marks journal_id required for type in (cash, bank)
# and both it and outstanding_account_id are empty on all five

point_of_sale:pos.payment.method.is_cash_count
# NOTHING TO DO: it was only ever a stored echo of type. 19.0's
# _compute_is_cash_count is `pm.is_cash_count = pm.type == 'cash'`, and the
# migrated table agrees exactly -- true on ids 1,3,5,7,9, precisely the rows
# that came out type='cash'. 20.0 drops the column and asks `pm.type == 'cash'`
# directly, so the information is already carried by type

point_of_sale:pos.payment.method.split_transactions
# NOTHING TO DO: 20.0 removes the concept along with the accounting path that
# used it. 19.0's "Identify Customer" forced a partner and split the closing
# entry per customer; grep for split_transactions across the whole 20.0 addons
# tree returns nothing, 20.0 having moved to per-order sale_move_ids /
# refund_move_ids. All 10 rows are false in any case

point_of_sale:pos.payment.method.company_id
# NOTHING TO DO: the NOT NULL applied cleanly because every row genuinely had a
# company, checked against two independent references. All 10 rows are filled
# (companies 1-5, two methods each); each row's company_id equals its journal's
# company_id where a journal is set, and equals the single company in
# account_account_res_company_rel for its receivable_account_id on every row.
# 19.0 already defaulted company_id to env.company

point_of_sale:pos.config.iface_print_skip_screen
# NOTHING TO DO: 20.0 drops the flag and keeps nothing equivalent. 19.0 skipped
# the receipt screen only when both flags were on (order_payment_validation.js);
# 20.0's replacement reads iface_print_auto alone (pos_config.js `get
# autoPrint()`), and grep for iface_print_skip_screen across 20.0 returns
# nothing. A config with auto-print on and preview-skip off will now skip, and
# there is no 20.0 field in which to say otherwise. Moot on this row --
# iface_print_auto is false, so the flag was already inert

point_of_sale:pos.order.last_order_preparation_change
# NOTHING TO DO: 20.0 replaces the JSON blob with pos.prep.order / pos.prep.line
# records, and the blob is live per-session kitchen bookkeeping nothing reads
# again. 20.0 rebuilds it from line quantities in update_last_order_change, so
# for a paid order there is nothing to show and for a draft one 20.0 re-derives
# it on the next change. pos_order is empty here and pos_restaurant, which owns
# kitchen printing, is uninstalled

point_of_sale:pos.session.cash_register_balance_start
# NOTHING TO DO -- DECLINED, not overlooked. 20.0's successor is opening_balance
# and it is NOT stored: related='bank_statement_id.balance_start', with
# bank_statement_id itself new in 20.0. The only place a script could write the
# opening count is account_bank_statement.balance_start of a statement that does
# not exist for any migrated session, and creating those means fabricating
# accounting records to hold a display value. The 19.0 number is not destroyed
# -- the cash_register_balance_start column survives with its values

point_of_sale:pos.category.active
# NOTHING TO DO: 19.0's pos.category had no archiving of any kind, so every 19.0
# category was visible and the default True is the only value that reproduces

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## website_sale -- NOT re-measured. The module is uninstalled in erp_mig20test,
## product_public_category does not exist there, and the seed the bootstrap
## measured against is gone. Every count quoted below is the bootstrap's own
## recording; the reasoning is from 19.0 and 20.0 source. Re-check against a
## database with website_sale installed before relying on the SCRIPT NEEDED
## lines.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

website_sale:website.contact_us_link_url
# SCRIPT NEEDED: a rename, and a default that silently overwrites it if nobody
# renames it. 19.0: contact_us_button_url = Char(translate=True,
# default="/contactus") (models/website.py:104). 20.0: contact_us_link_url =
# Char(translate=True, default="/contactus") (models/website.py:92), read by
# _get_contact_us_url() at :1213 -- same purpose, new name. Because the new
# column is created with its default, a site that pointed the button at /help
# or an external form gets "/contactus" back while its own value sits in the DEL
# column. pre-migration must openupgrade.rename_fields website
# contact_us_button_url -> contact_us_link_url before the ORM adds the column,
# which also carries the jsonb translations both versions store

website_sale:website.show_category_description
# SCRIPT NEEDED: the setting moved from per-category to per-website, and 20.0's
# default silently re-enables it. 19.0 held show_category_title /
# show_category_description / align_category_content on product.public.category
# (models/product_public_category.py:75-91), read off the browsed category
# (views/templates.xml:538-540); 20.0 holds all three on website
# (models/website.py:290-308) and reads website.show_category_*
# (templates/shop_page_templates.xml:144-146). The ORM wrote default True into
# show_category_description and left the other two NULL, a falsy default not
# being written. So a site that unticked "Show Description" gets descriptions
# back, and one that ticked "Show Title" loses titles. post-migration should set
# each website's three flags from the 19.0 columns of the categories that
# website shows, when those categories agree, and REPORT the websites whose
# categories disagree -- one website-wide flag cannot faithfully answer for
# categories that differ, and claiming a value nobody chose is worse than
# reporting it

website_sale:product.public.category.show_category_title
# SCRIPT NEEDED: this column is the only record of a per-category choice that
# 20.0 now keeps once per website, and post-migration has to read it. 19.0 wrote
# the three flags through the /shop/config/category route
# (controllers/main.py:1872); 20.0 writes them through /shop/config/website and
# has no per-category route left. This line's part is to keep the column
# readable -- rename it to its legacy name in pre-migration, as this branch
# already does for product.image.product_variant_id. The aggregation itself is
# under website.show_category_description above

website_sale:website.show_product_reference_price
# SCRIPT NEEDED: the $/kg switch moved from a feature group to a per-website
# boolean, and the new column starts False. 19.0 gated the reference price on
# the group alone -- _is_feature_enabled('website_sale.group_show_uom_price')
# put base_unit_price into combination_info (product_template.py:675). 20.0
# keeps the group but ALSO requires the website flag: product_template.py:765
# and :1035 only add base_unit_price when website.show_product_reference_price.
# With the flag False everywhere, a 19.0 site that had "Base Unit Price" on
# loses $/kg on the tiles, the product page and the cart. post-migration should
# set it TRUE on every website when the 19.0 feature was on -- base.group_user
# implies group_show_uom_price in res_groups_implied_rel, which is what
# _is_feature_enabled tested

website_sale:website.add_to_cart_action
# NOTHING TO DO: 20.0 removes the preference outright and there is no field to
# carry it into. Every piece of the 19.0 wiring is gone -- no field on website,
# no 'add_to_cart_action' session key in ir_http, no "Add to Cart" radio in
# res_config_settings_views, and cart_service.js no longer tests
# session.add_to_cart_action; in 20.0 shouldRedirectToCart comes only from
# isBuyNow or an explicit options.goToCart. A site that chose 'go_to_cart'
# loses that behaviour and no 20.0 field could record the choice. The 19.0
# column is left for database_cleanup

website_sale:account.move.website_id
# NOTHING TO DO: the same stored column, minus its compute. 19.0 declared it
# compute='_compute_website_id', store=True, readonly=True and created the
# column by hand in _auto_init; 20.0 declares a plain stored readonly Many2one
# with the same comodel and help text. Dropping a compute neither moves nor
# rewrites what is already in account_move.website_id

website_sale:product.public.category.not_in_shop
# NOTHING TO DO: a new 20.0 concept with nothing in 19.0 to carry. It hides a
# category from the unfiltered /shop listing -- 20.0's controllers/main.py:573
# adds Domain("not_in_shop","=",False) where 19.0's :426 had only the parent
# test -- and _compute_not_in_shop only copies parent_id.not_in_shop, so a root
# category has no source and stays False, exactly 19.0's behaviour

website_sale:product.template.suggest_alternative_products
# NOTHING TO DO: a flag for 20.0's new "Automate suggested products" cron, with
# no 19.0 counterpart. _compute_suggest_alternative_products sets it to `not
# template.alternative_product_ids` whenever
# _is_automate_suggested_product_feature_enabled() is false, and that tests a
# group 20.0 introduces -- so it is off right after an upgrade and the computed
# column states the 19.0 fact: alternative products were either chosen by hand
# or never chosen

website_sale:res.company.free_order_label
# NOTHING TO DO: 19.0 had no field -- the label was a literal in the template,
# views/templates.xml:3425 `<t t-set="submit_button_label">Confirm Order</t>` in
# the zero-total branch. 20.0 moves it to res.company with default="Confirm
# Order" (models/res_company.py:10). The new column's default reproduces the
# 19.0 wording word for word

website_sale:sale.order.assigned_website_id
# NOTHING TO DO: 20.0 fills it itself from a column 19.0 already had.
# _compute_assigned_website_id is @api.depends("website_id") and copies
# website_id onto every row when the stored column is added
# (models/sale_order.py:69-72); website_id is unchanged in 20.0. The compute is
# write-once, which is what lets a user retarget an order later

website_sale:website.prevent_sale_for
# NOTHING TO DO for this field: its default already says what 19.0 said. 19.0
# had one boolean, prevent_zero_price_sale. 20.0 splits it into the gate
# prevent_sale, this selection (default 'zero_price') and
# prevent_sale_for_categories; _prevent_product_sale() returns False unless
# prevent_sale is set and only then applies the zero-price test
# (models/website.py:1180-1204). 'zero_price' is 19.0's only mode. The choice a
# 19.0 administrator actually made lives in prevent_sale, which the mechanical
# marker wrongly reports as settled -- it is the successor of
# prevent_zero_price_sale and deserves a pre-migration rename

website_sale:website.rating_email_template_id
# NOTHING TO DO: 19.0 has no post-order rating feature to carry. Nothing named
# rating_email_template_id, rating_email_delay, send_order_rating_emails or
# sale.order.is_rating_email_sent exists in 19.0's website_sale. The uniform
# value is the field's own default, prepopulated for a feature that stays off:
# send_order_rating_emails defaults to False and sale_order.py:1210 only sends
# when a template is set on a website that has the feature on
